subject: embarrassingly incorrect statement in ez documentation (version 3.0 and earlier)

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: embarrassingly incorrect statement in ez documentation (version 3.0 and earlier)
parts:
An astute user just made me aware that in the documentation to
ezANOVA's output, I wrote the following:

"p p-value (probability of the null hypothesis given the data)."

Of course, this is completely backwards! The p-value is the
probability of the data (or data even more extreme) under the null
hypothesis.

I hope that the mis-statement was a result of late-night fuzziness,
but I shudder to think that I actually might have believed the
backwards version at the time of writing the original documentation.
Given the frequency (http://www.dgps.de/fachgruppen/methoden/mpr-
online/issue16/art1/article.html) of p-value misinterpretation, if I
did indeed believe the backwards interpretation I would not be alone.

To turn this embarrassment around as an opportunity to preach, I think
this really exemplifies a strong argument against null hypothesis
testing: we don't understand it and by our misinterpretations it's
clearly the case that we want it to give us information (usually an
index of the strength of evidence for/against a given hypothesis) that
it cannot. In contrast, likelihood ratios *do* give us the information
we want.
